title: Surface Areas and Volumes of Solid Figures
summary: Solids do not lie in one plane. The surface area is the area of the boundary of the solid; the volume is the space it encloses. Curved surface area (CSA) is the area of the curved part only; total surface area (TSA) includes the flat faces too. 1 m³ = 1000 litres; 1 litre = 1000 cm³.

Cuboid l × b × h: TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl), volume = lbh, diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²), area of four walls = 2(l + b)h. Cube of edge a: TSA = 6a², volume = a³, diagonal = a√3. Two cubes of edge a joined end to end form a cuboid 2a × a × a.

Right circular cylinder of radius r and height h: CSA = 2πrh, TSA = 2πr(h + r), volume = πr²h. A rectangular sheet rolled along its length forms a cylinder whose circumference is that length (66 cm sheet ⇒ 2πr = 66, r = 10.5 cm). Hollow cylinder (pipe) with outer radius R and inner r: volume of metal = πh(R² − r²).
Right circular cone of radius r, height h and slant height l: l² = r² + h²; CSA = πrl, TSA = πr(l + r), volume = ⅓πr²h. A cylinder with the same base and height holds 3 times the volume of the cone.
Sphere of radius r: surface area = 4πr², volume = (4/3)πr³. Hemisphere: CSA = 2πr², TSA = 3πr², volume = (2/3)πr³. Hollow sphere with outer radius R and inner r: volume = (4/3)π(R³ − r³).

When a solid is melted and recast, the volume stays the same: number of small solids = volume of the big solid ÷ volume of one small solid. For a solid made of two shapes (a cone on a hemisphere, a cylinder with a hemispherical end) add the volumes, and add only the outer curved surfaces for the surface area. Use π = 22/7 unless told to use 3.14.

objective: Write True or False: (i) The surface area of a cube of edge a is 6a². (ii) The total surface area of a cone is πrl.

(i) True: six square faces of area a² each.
(ii) False: πrl is the curved surface only; TSA = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r).

vsa: A solid metallic sphere of radius 21 cm is melted and recast into small cones of radius 7 cm and height 3 cm. Find the number of cones.

Volume of sphere = (4/3)π × 21³ = (4/3)π × 9261 = 12348π.
Volume of one cone = ⅓π × 7² × 3 = 49π.
Number of cones = 12348π ÷ 49π = 252.

sa: A cube and a cuboid have the same volume; the cuboid's sides are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 4. The difference in the cost of polishing them at ₹5 per m² is ₹80. Find their volume.

Cuboid sides x, 2x, 4x: volume 8x³, so the cube has edge 2x.
Cuboid TSA = 2(2x² + 8x² + 4x²) = 28x²; cube TSA = 6(2x)² = 24x².
Difference 4x² × 5 = 80 ⇒ x² = 4 ⇒ x = 2 m.
Volume = 8x³ = 64 m³.
A hollow cylindrical pipe has external radius 9 cm and length 14 cm. The metal used is 748 cm³. Find the thickness of the metal.

Volume of metal = πh(R² − r²) = 22/7 × 14 × (81 − r²) = 44(81 − r²).
44(81 − r²) = 748 ⇒ 81 − r² = 17 ⇒ r² = 64 ⇒ r = 8 cm.
Thickness = 9 − 8 = 1 cm.

Cylinder: π × 6² × 15 = 540π.
One cone: ⅓π × 3² × 12 = 36π.
Number = 540π ÷ 36π = 15 cones.
A solid toy is a hemisphere surmounted by a cone. The cone's height is 2 cm and the base diameter is 4 cm. Find the volume and surface area of the toy. (π = 22/7)

r = 2 cm, cone height h = 2 cm, slant height l = √(4 + 4) = 2√2 ≈ 2.83 cm.
Volume = ⅓πr²h + (2/3)πr³ = ⅓π × 4 × 2 + (2/3)π × 8 = 8π/3 + 16π/3 = 8π ≈ 25.14 cm³.
Surface = cone CSA + hemisphere CSA = πrl + 2πr² = π × 2 × 2.83 + 2π × 4 = 17.78 + 25.14 ≈ 42.92 cm².

A milk tanker is a cylinder of diameter 2 m and length 4.2 m. It supplies its milk to two booths in the ratio 3 : 2. One booth has a cuboidal vessel with base area 3.96 m² and the other a cylindrical vessel of radius 1 m. Find the level of milk in each.

Tanker volume = π × 1² × 4.2 = 22/7 × 4.2 = 13.2 m³.
Shares: 3/5 × 13.2 = 7.92 m³ and 2/5 × 13.2 = 5.28 m³.
Cuboidal vessel (gets 7.92): level = 7.92 ÷ 3.96 = 2 m.
Cylindrical vessel (gets 5.28): level = 5.28 ÷ (22/7 × 1²) = 1.68 m.
